title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Image | Page 10
text:
[IMAGE] This image appears to be a representation of the structure of a **micelle**, which is a key concept in the topic of **surface chemistry** and **colloids**.

A micelle is formed when **amphiphilic molecules** (molecules with both hydrophilic and hydrophobic parts) are added to water. The image likely illustrates how the **hydrophobic tails** of these molecules cluster together in the center to avoid water, while the **hydrophilic heads** face outward, interacting with the water molecules. This arrangement minimizes repulsion and stabilizes the structure.
Source: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry, Page 10

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Image | Page 15
text:
[IMAGE] This image illustrates the concept of crystal field splitting in transition metal complexes. It begins by showing a free metal ion (M) with its degenerate d orbitals (equal in energy), labeled as \(d_{xy}\), \(d_{xz}\), \(d_{yz}\), \(d_{x^2-y^2}\), and \(d_{z^2}\). When ligands (L) approach the metal ion in an octahedral arrangement, the energies of these d orbitals split into two sets: a lower energy \(t_{2g}\) set (consisting of \(d_{xy}\), \(d_{xz}\), and \(d_{yz}\)) and a higher energy \(e_g\) set (consisting of \(d_{x^2-y^2}\) and \(d_{z^2}\)). The diagram also shows the average energy shift and the magnitude of splitting (\(\Delta_o\)), which is crucial for understanding the electronic configuration and properties of coordination compounds.
Source: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry, Page 15

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Image | Page 16
text:
[IMAGE] This image illustrates the concept of crystal field splitting in transition metal complexes, specifically comparing the energy levels of d orbitals in a free ion versus those in a tetrahedral crystal field.

In a free ion, the five d orbitals have equal energy. When placed in a tetrahedral crystal field (surrounded by ligands), these d orbitals split into two distinct energy levels: a lower energy level consisting of the \(d_{xy}, d_{yz}, d_{zx}\) orbitals, and a higher energy level consisting of the \(d_{z^2}\) and \(d_{x^2-y^2}\) orbitals. The energy difference between these split levels is denoted by \(\Delta\), which represents the crystal field splitting energy in a tetrahedral environment.
Source: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry, Page 16
